content.content:
# Handoff: how caliper-docgen uses the `tsrs` checker, and what to dig into

Written 2026-11-20 from measurements on caliper `main` (c633fbc6 plus docs). Nothing here is merged work; it is evidence and a map.

## What we use

- **`tsrs`** is `oxc-project/tsrs` (Apache-2.0), a Rust port of the TypeScript 7.1 checker. It is upstream, not ours. We pin the crates exactly: `tsrs_api`, `tsrs_vfs`, `tsrs_core` `=0.24.0` (TypeScript commit `3e9236361fa9`, `typescript@7.1.0-beta`). Pin changes are deliberate, never through dependabot (ADR 0026).
- **Linked, not spawned** (ADR 0026, trail 369): we link the crates and ask `tsrs_api::Session` in process. Measured then: the same recorded Chakra answer, 3,776 requests, took 141 ms in process against 367 ms over a pipe.
- **How we ask:** `crates/semantic/src/checker.rs` creates a `Session` on a thread of its own with a 512 MiB stack (a type 2,000 deep overflows a default stack and aborts the process). `Session::new(SessionOptions::new(cwd, bundled::lib_path(), fs, false))`. TypeScript's lib files (`lib.dom.d.ts`, ES libs) are bundled inside `tsrs_vfs`, not read from the project. `@types/react` and csstype are read from the project's `node_modules`.
- **`tsrs_api` is a port of TypeScript's JSON API server** (`session.go`, `proto.go`). Every request is a JSON method plus params; every answer is `Response::Json(String)`. Our `crates/semantic/src/rpc.rs` builds params as `serde_json::Value`, serializes them, the handler parses them again, answers as text, and we parse that. Batching exists (`batchRequests`, `rpc.batch(..)` in `declared.rs`).
- **Who calls it:** `component.rs` (per component: props, `composes` walk, `leave_to_layers`), `convert.rs` (the type converter, memoized by type id within one snapshot), `declared.rs` (declarations by name, batched), `instantiate.rs` (generic component instantiation through a generated probe file; it calls `getSemanticDiagnostics` on that file), `lib.rs` (scheduler, prefetch, kept answers). Docs: `docs/type-checker-integration.md`, ADR 0022, ADR 0026, `docs/gate-measurements.md`.

## Measurements (release builds, machine at load 11 to 22; trust ratios and counts, not absolute times)

Cold default run (checker on, `--load-dependencies`, `--no-cache`), shadcn `apps/v4`, 2.06 s wall, 6.6 CPU-seconds:

| Phase (traced) | Span |
| --- | --- |
| structural parse and module resolution (about 20,000 resolver calls for 1,385 files) | 0 to 312 ms |
| unexplained before the first checker answer | 312 to 565 ms |
| about 1,800 component answers (about 0.6 ms each, 32,251 requests, mean 17.9 per component) | 565 to 1690 ms |
| merge and serialization of 4.7 MB JSON | to about 2 s |

Busy CPU by subsystem (profiling build, sampled from launch): allocation and copying 24.8%, JSON codec (checker IPC) 21.4%, `tsrs` checker work 14.5%, files and VFS 10.1%, tsrs parse, bind and symbols 6.9%, caliper core 4.6%, other 16.6%. About 60% of thread samples are idle waits.

Spike worker (instrumented `rpc.rs`, shadcn cold run):
- About 33.7k top-level requests plus 17.9k sub-requests inside 4,060 `batchRequests`. ---
name: tsrs-checker-handoff
description: 2026-11-20 briefing for the tsrs cold-start investigation — usage, key numbers, items 0-7, measuring rules (condensed; full copy was /tmp/claude-501/handoff-tsrs-checker.md)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Briefing (2026-11-20, main c633fbc6) for cutting cold-start cost of a default run (checker on, `--load-dependencies`) without changing output. tsrs = oxc-project/tsrs pinned `=0.24.0`, linked in process via `tsrs_api::Session` (JSON text requests/answers; `crates/semantic/src/rpc.rs`, `checker.rs` 512 MiB stack thread).

Key numbers (shadcn apps/v4 cold, 2.06 s wall, 6.6 CPU-s): ~33.7k top-level requests + 17.9k in 4,060 batches; handler 1,776 ms of which `getSemanticDiagnostics` (one call, `instantiate.rs:182` probe file) 797 ms, `getPropertiesOfType` 546 ms (193 MB of 212 MB responses, 684/1,708 repeats). Codec ≥450 ms. Chakra: 743k `isReadonlySymbol` sub-requests, `batchRequests` 3.6 s; ~28k of 59k requests identical repeats. Unexplained 312-565 ms gap before first answer. Resolver ~20k calls for 1,385 files.

Items in order: 0 Chakra `isReadonlySymbol` in `Converter::fields`; 0b per-run (method, params) memo; 1 probe `getSemanticDiagnostics`; 2 `getPropertiesOfType` payload; 3 requests/component (mean 17.9), type-id memo, batching loops; 4 draft upstream issue (typed Response / leaner getPropertiesOfType) — owner sends it; 5 tsrs hot spots (SymbolMap rehash, JsonMap::get_index_of, NodeIndexTable, stat cache); 6 the 250 ms gap; 7 resolver memo per (dir, specifier).

Measure: corpora in ~/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos; `target/release/caliper-docgen extract --src <dir> --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies --json` under `/usr/bin/time -l`; interleave main vs branch, best of 5-7, CPU time (user+sys), compare JSON minus `stats`; rerun a degraded run. Profiling: `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=none REDACTED`, `sample caliper-docgen 8 1 -wait -mayDie`.

Rules: no push/PR/upstream/merge; only small safe measured wins on own branch with failing-on-main test + CONTRIBUTING gate; no weekly oracle; build in worktree target/, delete multi-GB dirs after. Deliverable: report <700 words + table per item (measured, saving, effort, risk, order) + separate upstream issue draft. See [[run-the-oracle-sparingly]], [[measure-memory-and-time]], [[measurement-must-match-real-consumer]].

# Draft issue for oxc-project/tsrs (not sent; the owner sends it)

**Title:** In-process API: a typed result path and leaner symbol responses (`getPropertiesOfType` is 56% node handles)

We embed tsrs `0.24.0` in process through `tsrs_api::Session` to read component props for documentation (React, `@types/react`). Every request and answer crosses as JSON text even though both sides are Rust in one process. Measurements below are from release builds on five open-source corpora (shadcn `apps/v4`, Chakra UI, Mantine, Ant Design, React Spectrum).

## 1. Symbol responses repeat the absolute path four or more times

One `getPropertiesOfType` answer for a React props type (282 symbols) is 158 KB, about 560 bytes per symbol:

- `valueDeclaration` 28% and `declarations` 28% of the bytes: each node handle is `"<index>.<kind>.<absolute path>"`.
- `reference.file` carries the source-file descriptor with `fileName` and `path`, both absolute (another 9%).
- Per run on shadcn: 1,708 calls, 193 MB of responses from this method alone; handler time about 546 ms, much of it formatting and encoding these strings.

Asks, any of which would help:

- A request option (a field mask) to leave out `valueDeclaration`, `checkFlags` and `exportSymbol`, or to return compact references (`{ id, file: <nodeId> }`) instead of full descriptors.
- Node handles relative to a file id already sent (`"<index>.<kind>.#<fileNodeId>"`) when the file descriptor is in the same response.

## 2. A typed result path for in-process callers

`Response::Json(String)` means an embedding caller serializes params to text, the handler parses them, answers as text and the caller parses that. On shadcn: about 33.7k top-level requests plus 17.9k batched, 11 MB of requests and 212 MB of responses; the codec costs at least 450 ms (our side: encode 11 ms, validate 116 ms, decode 182 ms; tsrs side: decode 17 ms, marshal 120 ms).

Ask: a `Response` variant (or a sink) that hands back the structured `Value` (or typed structs) to an in-process caller, and a public way to call the existing handlers with a `Value` for params from outside the crate (today `dispatch::handle` needs a `CheckerHost`, and `Session`'s host is private).

## 3. `getSemanticDiagnostics` always uses the dedicated diagnostics checker

`handle_get_diagnostics` sets `CheckerLifetime::Diagnostics`, so a file checked through the API is checked by checker 0, a fresh checker that shares no resolved types with the persistent (`API`) checker every other request uses. For a caller that asks diagnostics of one small file and then queries the same types, the diagnostics pass costs a second cold checker: 0.64 to 1.54 s and up to 570 MiB of peak RSS on our corpora.

Ask: an option on `getSemanticDiagnostics` (`checker: "api"`) to check the file with the persistent checker, or document that the two never share work.

## Not an ask, for information

`NodeIndexTable::get_index` re-derives node ids on each binary-search probe; building handles for many declarations of one file could use a per-file `(node id → index)` map.

# Cold-start cost of a checker run: findings (2026-11-20, main c633fbc6)

Release builds, `extract --no-cache --load-dependencies`, five corpora. The machine was at load 20 to 105, so I read best-of-5 interleaved CPU and ratios; absolute walls are inflated. Output was compared as JSON with `stats` dropped. Raw instrumentation: `experiment-instrumentation.patch` (env-gated, not for merge).

## Found on the way: runs that randomly lose the checker (fixed on a branch)

The briefing's "degraded checker run" is a bug in caliper, not load. `heap::committed` casts mimalloc's signed `committed.current` (`stats.c:457`) to unsigned. The counter dips below zero while threads give memory back, reads as 16 EiB, and the 8 GiB budget stops the run: Chakra printed "the heap held 17592186044414 MiB" and left all 620 components structural in 2 of 3 runs, finishing in a third of the time. Any timing taken on main may include such runs. With the clamp: 0 degraded in 65 runs. Branch `fix/heap-meter-signed-commit` (local, not pushed): one function, two tests (one fails with the old cast), changeset.

## Item 1: `getSemanticDiagnostics` on the probe file is almost wholly avoidable

Why it costs so much: tsrs answers it with `CheckerLifetime::Diagnostics` (`tsrs_api/src/program.rs:63`), which is the pool's dedicated diagnostics checker (`tsrs_project/src/checkerpool.rs:431`), a fresh checker on the layered program. Every other request uses the persistent API checker, so nothing the diagnostics pass resolves is reused by the probe reads. It also runs after every lane, on the critical path.

What it found: on all five corpora (66 probes) every line it flagged (15) was already rejected by `arguments_keep_their_meaning`; the errors were all `Cannot find name` for a printed default. Skipping it gives identical components; only the fallback reason text changes (it names a different cause).

Saving (diagnostics on → skipped): antd CPU 3.05 → 1.79 s, wall 1.60 → 0.38; spectrum 4.65 → 3.49, 1.63 → 0.55; shadcn 6.32 → 5.63, 1.61 → 0.99; mantine 3.50 → 3.12; chakra 11.64 → 11.13. Peak RSS: antd 953 → 381 MiB, spectrum 759 → 498, shadcn 874 → 758.

Recommendation: drop the call and keep the guarantee with what the API checker already holds: reject a probe whose argument alias or `CaliperProbe` type is the `error` intrinsic (`intrinsic_name == "error"`), and phrase the reason from that ("`FieldValues` does not resolve where the instantiation is written"). The ADR-era doc (`docs/type-checker-integration.md:201`) promises diagnostics-based detection, so the doc and `tests/instantiate.rs` fixtures (`generic-foreign-error`) change too. I did not implement it: it changes a documented contract and wants the owner's decision.

## Items 0 and 0b (handed to the request-reduction worker; measured here)

- Skipping `isReadonlySymbol` on Chakra: identical output (not one of its answers is true), CPU 16.1–17.2 → 14.5–14.7 s. It cannot simply go: spectrum has 4,356 readonly fields, antd 269, shadcn 210. Only asking for shown rows, or a type-id memo of `fields`, is the route.
- A naive (method, params) memo of every read: identical output on all five; CPU −4 to −20% (mantine 4.74 → 3.81, shadcn 8.06 → 7.49, chakra 16.4 → 15.6, antd ≈ 0). But it costs memory: +89 MiB shadcn, +360 MiB chakra, +95 MiB mantine, because it keeps every answer. Memo only small, highly repeated answers (`getBaseTypes`, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType`, `getTargetOfType`, signatures, parameters) and props decoded per type id. Repeats are within one snapshot (lanes have their own), so a per-`Rpc` memo catches them.

## Item 2: `getPropertiesOfType` payload

One answer: 282 symbols, 158 KB, 560 B each. `valueDeclaration` 28% and `declarations` 28% (each handle embeds the absolute path), file descriptor `fileName`+`path` 9%. We read neither `valueDeclaration` nor `checkFlags`. Caller side: 650 of shadcn's calls are exact repeats (98 MB), removable by the memo above. Leaner encoding is upstream (draft issue).

## Items 4 to 7

- 4: issue drafted (`tsrs-upstream-issue-draft.md`): field mask / compact references, a typed result path, and an option to check a file with the API checker.
- 5: `JsonMap::get_index_of` is linear only for small maps (large ones are hashed), so its samples measure JSON volume. `NodeIndexTable::get_index` re-derives node ids per binary-search probe; minor next to formatting a path string per handle. Not profiled further.
- 6: not measured (load reached 105). Reading: the program opens on its own thread (`start_early`) during structural work, so the gap is most likely program build not finished; `-vv` logs `program_ms` to confirm.
- 7: not measured. Candidate: `ModuleResolvers::new` builds two `Resolver::new`, so the two share no filesystem or tsconfig cache; `main.clone_with_options(..)` shares it (one line).

## Table

- Heap meter wrap: measured 2/3 Chakra runs degraded → 0/65 · saving: correct output, reliable timings · effort XS · risk low · **done on branch, order 1**
- Item 1 probe diagnostics: measured on 5 corpora · −0.4 to −1.3 s CPU, −0.5 to −1.2 s wall, up to −570 MiB · effort S (code, doc, fixtures) · risk low-medium (contract change) · **order 2**
- Item 0 readonly: measured Chakra · up to −2 s CPU there · effort M · risk low if limited to shown rows · order 3 (other worker)
- Item 0b/3 memo: measured 5 corpora · −4 to −20% CPU · effort S · risk memory, bounded by memoizing small answers only · order 4 (other worker)
- Item 2 payload: measured one answer · ~55% of bytes upstream; repeats caller-side via memo · effort S here, upstream there · order 5
- Item 7 resolver cache share: not measured · unknown, likely tens of ms · effort XS · risk low · order 6
- Item 6 gap: not measured · effort S to profile · order 7
- Items 4 and 5 upstream: drafted, not sent · owner's call

Give me a rundown

One change is measured and ready locally. The next priorities are readonly queries and request memoization; the JSON-boundary prototype remains with the other worker.

- Diagnostics fix: caliper sent file, but tsrs expects files. That accidentally checked the whole program instead of just the generated probe file. Correcting it reduced shadcn’s diagnostics call from about 803 ms to 2.35 ms, while preserving output and fallback explanations.

| Corpus | Best CPU before → after | Saving |
|---|---|---|
| shadcn | 6.48 → 6.03 s | 6.9% |
| Mantine | 3.47 → 3.18 s | 8.4% |
| Chakra | 12.57 → 11.87 s | 5.6% |

The machine was loaded. Degraded Chakra runs were excluded.

- Readonly is a strong local target: Chakra made 745,088 readonly queries, but only 210,012 were distinct within their snapshot. Symbol flags alone cannot reliably replace them. Memoization could eliminate roughly 535,000 queries. Readonly-only batches account for about 134 MB sent and 34 MB received; the earlier 261 MB response figure includes other work.
- Repeated requests mostly cross components: Chakra repeated 20,911 calls across the five proposed memo methods. A shared, snapshot-scoped memo is promising. Its runtime benefit and response-invalidation rules still need verification.
- Avoiding JSON text looks feasible through existing APIs: public checker::dispatch::handle retains the real handlers and takes/returns JSON values through a custom CheckerHost. The session registry is publicly accessible. Private file-cache and node helpers still need careful handling. The other worker’s prototype should establish compatibility and net savings; 450 ms is an inherited codec estimate, not a demonstrated speedup.
- Lower-priority findings: field trimming alone saves about 23% of shadcn’s property bytes and 8% of Chakra’s. Resolver memos and indexed lookups already exist. The fixed 250 ms startup gap was not reproduced.

content.text:
Codex's item 1 fix is the one to take, and its excluded "degraded Chakra runs" come from a separate caliper bug that I've fixed on its own branch.

**Item 1 (Codex is right).** Caliper sends `"file"`, but tsrs's `handle_get_diagnostics` only narrows to a file when it gets `"files"`. Otherwise it checks the whole program. That is the main cost; I had put it down to the separate diagnostics checker tsrs uses. Keep `perf/probe-file-diagnostics`: it keeps the documented contract and the fallback reasons. My measurements are the upper bound of that fix. Skipping the call entirely gave identical components on all five corpora, saving 0.4–1.3 s CPU and up to 570 MiB peak memory (antd 953 → 381 MiB). On all five, every line diagnostics flagged was already rejected by the existing argument check.

**The new bug: runs that randomly lose the checker.** caliper reads mimalloc's committed-bytes counter as unsigned. The counter can briefly go below zero, so −2 MiB reads as about 16 EiB and passes the 8 GiB heap budget. On Chakra that left all 620 components without checker results in 2 of 3 runs, and those runs finish about three times faster. Any timings on main may include such runs, including Codex's.
- **Fix:** a below-zero reading now counts as nothing. After the fix: 0 bad runs in 65. Commit `e68d07e4` on `fix/heap-meter-signed-commit`, local and not pushed.
- **Tests:** two tests and a changeset. One test fails if the old cast is put back.
- **Checks:** `just lint doc-check machete typos` all passed. `lint`, `doc-check` and `machete` passed on the run before `typos` was rerun; that first failure was only in my untracked notes, which I fixed.
